Section 1: Concept of Programming (Questions 1 to 25)

Instructions, Programs, Programming Languages, Procedural/Non-procedural, Structured Programming, OOP

Q1. What is an instruction in the context of programming?

A) A complete program B) A single command or operation given to the computer ✅ C) A collection of programs D) A type of programming language

Q2. Which of the following is an example of an instruction?

A) `a = b + c;` ✅ B) Microsoft Word C) Windows 10 D) A keyboard

Q3. What is a program?

A) A single instruction B) A set of instructions written to solve a specific problem ✅ C) A type of hardware D) An operating system

Q4. Which of the following is an example of a program?

A) `printf("Hello");` B) A calculator application that adds two numbers ✅ C) A CPU D) A mouse driver

Q5. Which of the following is a High-Level Language?

A) Machine Language B) Assembly Language C) C Language ✅ D) Binary Code

Q6. Which of the following is a Low-Level Language?

A) Python B) Java C) C++ D) Assembly Language ✅

Q7. What is Assembly Language?

A) A high-level language B) A low-level language that uses mnemonics ✅ C) A natural language D) A database language

Q8. Machine Language consists of:

A) English words B) 0s and 1s ✅ C) Mnemonics D) Symbols

Q9. Which type of programming language is closest to human language?

A) Low-Level Language B) Machine Language C) High-Level Language ✅ D) Assembly Language

Q10. What is Procedural Programming?

A) Programming using objects B) Programming using functions and procedures that operate on data ✅ C) Programming without any structure D) Programming using only assembly code

Q11. Which of the following is an example of a Procedural Language?

A) C ✅ B) Java C) Python (can be both, but C is pure procedural) D) C++

Q12. What is Non-Procedural Programming?

A) Programming that uses procedures B) Programming where the programmer specifies what to do, not how to do it ✅ C) Programming that uses only assembly D) Programming without functions

Q13. Which of the following is an example of a Non-Procedural Language?

A) C B) FORTRAN C) SQL ✅ D) Pascal

Q14. What is Structured Programming?

A) Programming without any structure B) Programming using only goto statements C) Programming using sequence, selection, and iteration ✅ D) Programming using objects

Q15. Which of the following is a key feature of Structured Programming?

A) Use of goto statements B) No functions allowed C) Use of loops and conditional statements ✅ D) Only sequential execution

Q16. Who is credited with developing Structured Programming concepts?

A) Dennis Ritchie B) Edsger Dijkstra ✅ C) Alan Turing D) Bill Gates

Q17. What is Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)?

A) Programming using only functions B) Programming using objects that contain data and methods ✅ C) Programming without classes D) Programming using only global variables

Q18. Which of the following is a core concept of OOP?

A) Inheritance ✅ B) Procedures C) Recursion D) Global variables

Q19. Which of the following is NOT a feature of OOP?

A) Encapsulation B) Polymorphism C) Inheritance D) Goto statements ✅

Q20. Which of the following is an example of an Object-Oriented Language?

A) C B) FORTRAN C) Java ✅ D) Assembly

Q21. What does encapsulation in OOP mean?

A) Hiding internal details and protecting data from direct access ✅ B) Using multiple functions C) Creating loops D) Using global variables

Q22. What is polymorphism in OOP?

A) One name having multiple forms ✅ B) One function performing one task C) One object belonging to one class D) Data hiding

Q23. What is inheritance in OOP?

A) Creating new classes from existing ones ✅ B) Creating new functions C) Defining loops D) Using pointers

Q24. Which of the following is TRUE about Structured Programming?

A) It uses goto statements extensively. B) It uses only one function. C) It emphasizes top-down approach. ✅ D) It doesn't use loops.

Q25. Which paradigm focuses on "what to do" rather than "how to do it"?

A) Procedural Programming B) Non-Procedural Programming ✅ C) Structured Programming D) Object-Oriented Programming

Section 2: Algorithm Fundamentals (Questions 26 to 80)

Definition, Characteristics, Recursive/Non-recursive Algorithms, Flowchart, Pseudo code, Efficiency, Complexity, Asymptotic Notations

Q26. What is an algorithm?

A) A programming language B) A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem ✅ C) A type of data structure D) A computer program

Q27. Which of the following is a characteristic of a good algorithm?

A) Ambiguity B) Infinite loops C) Definiteness ✅ D) Randomness

Q28. An algorithm must have:

A) Zero inputs B) Infinite steps C) Finiteness ✅ D) No output

Q29. What is a recursive algorithm?

A) An algorithm that uses loops B) An algorithm that calls itself ✅ C) An algorithm with no output D) An algorithm that never terminates

Q30. What is a non-recursive algorithm?

A) An algorithm that calls itself B) An algorithm that uses iteration instead of recursion ✅ C) An algorithm without any steps D) An algorithm with only one step

Q31. Which of the following is an example of a recursive algorithm?

A) Factorial calculation using recursion ✅ B) Factorial calculation using a for loop C) Sum of two numbers D) Finding maximum of three numbers

Q32. What is the base case in a recursive algorithm?

A) The condition that stops the recursion ✅ B) The recursive call C) The first step D) The last step

Q33. What is a flowchart?

A) A programming language B) A graphical representation of an algorithm ✅ C) A type of data D) A compiler

Q34. Which symbol is used in a flowchart to represent the start/end?

A) Rectangle B) Diamond C) Oval/Ellipse ✅ D) Parallelogram

Q35. Which symbol is used in a flowchart to represent a decision?

A) Rectangle B) Diamond ✅ C) Oval D) Parallelogram

Q36. Which symbol represents an input/output operation in a flowchart?

A) Rectangle B) Diamond C) Oval D) Parallelogram ✅

Q37. What is pseudo code?

A) A programming language B) A simplified, informal description of an algorithm ✅ C) A flowchart D) A compiler

Q38. Which of the following is an example of pseudo code?

A) `if (x > 0) then print x` ✅ B) `int main()` C) `MOV AX, 5` D) `010101`

Q39. What is the efficiency of an algorithm?

A) How long the algorithm takes to run B) How much memory the algorithm uses C) How well the algorithm uses resources ✅ D) How many lines of code it has

Q40. What is time complexity?

A) The amount of memory used by an algorithm B) The time taken by an algorithm to run ✅ C) The number of variables used D) The number of functions used

Q41. What is space complexity?

A) The time taken by an algorithm B) The amount of memory used by an algorithm ✅ C) The number of loops used D) The number of recursive calls

Q42. Which complexity measure focuses on the memory used?

A) Time complexity B) Space complexity ✅ C) Both D) Neither

Q43. What does Big O notation represent?

A) Exact running time of an algorithm B) Upper bound of running time ✅ C) Lower bound of running time D) Average case running time

Q44. What does Big Omega (Ω) notation represent?

A) Upper bound B) Lower bound ✅ C) Tight bound D) Average case

Q45. What does Big Theta (Θ) notation represent?

A) Upper bound B) Lower bound C) Tight bound (both upper and lower) ✅ D) Best case

Q46. An algorithm with time complexity O(n) means:

A) It takes exactly n seconds B) Running time grows linearly with input size ✅ C) Running time is constant D) Running time grows quadratically

Q47. What is the time complexity of a simple for loop that runs n times?

A) O(1) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(log n)

Q48. What is the time complexity of a nested for loop (both running n times)?

A) O(n) B) O(n²) ✅ C) O(log n) D) O(1)

Q49. What is the time complexity of binary search?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(1)

Q50. What is the time complexity of linear search?

A) O(1) B) O(log n) C) O(n) ✅ D) O(n²)

Q51. What is the time complexity of bubble sort?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) C) O(n²) ✅ D) O(n log n)

Q52. What is the time complexity of merge sort?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) C) O(n²) D) O(n log n) ✅

Q53. Which complexity is considered the most efficient?

A) O(n²) B) O(2ⁿ) C) O(log n) ✅ D) O(n)

Q54. What is the worst-case complexity of an algorithm?

A) Best case running time B) Maximum running time for any input ✅ C) Average running time D) Minimum running time

Q55. What is the best-case complexity of an algorithm?

A) Maximum running time B) Minimum running time for any input ✅ C) Average running time D) Worst-case running time

Q56. What is the average-case complexity?

A) Running time for the best input B) Running time for the worst input C) Average running time for all possible inputs ✅ D) Running time for a specific input

Q57. Which asymptotic notation provides a tight bound?

A) Big O B) Big Omega C) Big Theta ✅ D) Little o

Q58. If an algorithm is O(n²), it means:

A) It will never take more than n² steps ✅ B) It always takes exactly n² steps C) It takes at least n² steps D) It takes log n steps

Q59. If an algorithm is Ω(n), it means:

A) It will never take more than n steps B) It will take at least n steps ✅ C) It always takes exactly n steps D) It takes constant time

Q60. Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of an algorithm?

A) Input B) Output C) Randomness ✅ D) Finiteness

Q61. What is the importance of algorithm efficiency?

A) It makes the program longer B) It helps in better utilization of resources ✅ C) It makes the code more complex D) It increases the number of bugs

Q62. What is the difference between time complexity and space complexity?

A) Time complexity measures memory, space measures time B) Time complexity measures time, space measures memory ✅ C) Both measure time D) Both measure memory

Q63. What is the time complexity of accessing an array element by index?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) C) O(1) ✅ D) O(n²)

Q64. What is the time complexity of inserting an element at the end of an array?

A) O(1) ✅ B) O(n) C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Q65. What is the time complexity of inserting an element at the beginning of an array?

A) O(1) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Q66. Which of the following algorithms has the worst time complexity?

A) Linear search B) Binary search C) Bubble sort D) Exponential search (2ⁿ) ✅

Q67. What is the time complexity of factorial calculation using recursion?

A) O(1) B) O(log n) C) O(n) ✅ D) O(n²)

Q68. What is the space complexity of factorial calculation using recursion?

A) O(1) B) O(log n) C) O(n) ✅ (due to recursion stack) D) O(n²)

Q69. What is the time complexity of Fibonacci using recursion?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) C) O(2ⁿ) ✅ D) O(n²)

Q70. What is a pseudo-code used for?

A) Executing directly on a computer B) Planning and describing algorithms ✅ C) Compiling programs D) Debugging code

Q71. Which of the following is a disadvantage of pseudo-code?

A) Easy to understand B) Language independent C) Not executable on a computer ✅ D) Simple to write

Q72. A flowchart is used to:

A) Write code directly B) Visualize the flow of an algorithm ✅ C) Execute a program D) Compile code

Q73. What is the purpose of algorithm analysis?

A) To make the program longer B) To understand the efficiency and performance ✅ C) To add more bugs D) To make the program unreadable

Q74. Which notation describes the best-case performance?

A) Big O B) Big Omega ✅ C) Big Theta D) Little o

Q75. Which notation describes the worst-case performance?

A) Big O ✅ B) Big Omega C) Big Theta D) Little o

Q76. What is the time complexity of finding the maximum element in an array?

A) O(1) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(log n)

Q77. What is the time complexity of swapping two variables?

A) O(1) ✅ B) O(n) C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Q78. What is the time complexity of matrix multiplication (standard algorithm)?

A) O(n²) B) O(n³) ✅ C) O(n log n) D) O(n)

Q79. What is the space complexity of iterative factorial?

A) O(1) ✅ B) O(n) C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Q80. What is the space complexity of linear search?

A) O(1) ✅ B) O(n) C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Section 3: Introduction to Problem Solving (Questions 81 to 100)

Steps for Problem Solving (Analysing, Developing Algorithm, Coding, Testing, Debugging)

Q81. What is the first step in problem solving?

A) Coding B) Testing C) Analysing the problem ✅ D) Debugging

Q82. What is problem analysis?

A) Writing code for the problem B) Understanding the problem and its requirements ✅ C) Executing the program D) Fixing errors

Q83. After problem analysis, what is the next step?

A) Coding B) Testing C) Developing an algorithm ✅ D) Debugging

Q84. What is the third step in problem solving?

A) Problem analysis B) Algorithm development C) Coding/Implementation ✅ D) Testing

Q85. What is coding in problem solving?

A) Understanding the problem B) Writing the actual program code ✅ C) Testing the program D) Finding errors

Q86. What is the purpose of testing?

A) To write the program B) To find errors and verify correctness ✅ C) To design the algorithm D) To analyze the problem

Q87. What is debugging?

A) Writing code B) Testing the program C) Finding and fixing errors in the code ✅ D) Analyzing requirements

Q88. What is the correct order of problem-solving steps?

A) Coding → Testing → Debugging → Analysis B) Analysis → Algorithm → Coding → Testing → Debugging ✅ C) Testing → Coding → Analysis → Debugging D) Algorithm → Analysis → Coding → Testing

Q89. What is the difference between testing and debugging?

A) Testing writes code, debugging runs it B) Testing finds errors, debugging fixes them ✅ C) Testing fixes errors, debugging finds them D) They are the same thing

Q90. What is unit testing?

A) Testing the entire program at once B) Testing individual components or modules ✅ C) Testing the user interface D) Testing the hardware

Q91. What is system testing?

A) Testing individual modules B) Testing the entire integrated system ✅ C) Testing the algorithm D) Testing the documentation

Q92. What is a bug in programming?

A) An insect in the computer B) An error or flaw in the program ✅ C) A type of comment D) A programming language

Q93. What is the purpose of problem-solving steps?

A) To make coding more difficult B) To ensure systematic and efficient solution development ✅ C) To increase program size D) To add more bugs

Q94. Which step involves writing the actual program?

A) Problem analysis B) Algorithm design C) Coding ✅ D) Testing

Q95. What is the importance of testing?

A) It proves the program is perfect B) It helps find errors and ensures correct output ✅ C) It makes the program run slower D) It deletes the program

Q96. What is the final step in problem solving?

A) Problem analysis B) Algorithm development C) Coding D) Testing and Debugging ✅

Q97. What is an integrated development environment (IDE)?

A) A type of algorithm B) A software that provides tools for coding, testing, and debugging ✅ C) A programming language D) A flowchart symbol

Q98. What does debugging typically involve?

A) Writing new code B) Using tools to trace and fix errors ✅ C) Testing the algorithm D) Analyzing requirements

Q99. What is the difference between syntax errors and logical errors?

A) Syntax errors are logical, logical errors are syntax B) Syntax errors violate language rules, logical errors produce wrong output ✅ C) Both are same D) Syntax errors produce wrong output, logical errors violate rules

Q100. Which statement about problem solving is TRUE?

A) Coding is the most important step B) Analysis is unnecessary C) Testing is optional D) Each step is important for a successful solution ✅
